title: Compute supply-chain bottlenecks
scope: Eight documentary collection decisions: seven primary-supported samples plus one rights-only SK hynix candidate. Issuer-attributed disclosures do not independently validate physical output, installed fleets or usable compute. No source bytes or compiled historical series are included.
verification_disposition: Bounded review disposition complete; substantive SK hynix release/milestone verification remains held.
source_snapshot_limit: No exact upstream HTML/PDF byte identity is claimed. Direct artifact URLs, source locators and source-specific verification limits remain explicit.
third_party_rights: Original factual research metadata does not extend source grants. Acquisition permission and compiled extracted-data redistribution are separate unresolved questions; restrictions remain binding.
verdict: Retain eight new documentary collection families and prioritize TSMC, Micron and ASML. Seven collections have primary-supported samples; SK hynix remains rights-only with unverified milestones. One rights-gated ASML specification is deferred. No historical series, independent physical validation or usable-compute estimate is admitted.

interpretation_guards: Issuer disclosures establish reported claims, not independent factory conditions or usable compute.
Orders, commitments, backlog, capacity, output, shipments, installed stock and workload performance have different units/stages.
Revenue recognition is accounting, not a universal physical intermediate step.
Preserve units, fiscal/calendar periods, disclosure/filing dates, bounds, categorical qualifiers and source vintages.
No AI-only share from HPC revenue; no hardware count to FLOP/s, usable compute, capability score or p(doom).
Do not sum upstream/downstream units or period totals/constituents.
Unknowns, acquisition and reuse holds stay explicit; no source artifact redistribution authorized.
SEC hosting/financial audit is neither an issuer-content license nor independent physical validation.
